## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Vigaticchajātaka* (Ja 244) is a story of the Buddha's past lives included in the Jātaka collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The narrative was delivered by the Buddha while residing at Jetavana concerning a wandering turntail ascetic (*paribbājaka*) who traveled throughout the country [SuttaCentral]. In the commentary's concluding connection (*samodhāna*), the Buddha reveals that this contemporary ascetic was the very same wandering mendicant of the past, while the Bodhisatta was an ascetic (*tāpasa*) [Fausböll 1879]. The commentary elaborates on the insatiability of desire (*icchā hi anantagocarā*), which is never satisfied with what is gained, and praises the act of paying homage to those who have transcended craving, such as the Buddhas (*vigaticchā Buddhādayo*) [Fausböll 1879].
In V. Fausböll's edition of the Jātaka commentary, the tale is titled *Vīticchajātakam* in the text, with *Vigaticchajātakam* recorded as a variant reading in Burmese manuscripts [Fausböll 1879]. SuttaCentral records four modern translations of the work across four languages [SuttaCentral]. Neither curated parallels on SuttaCentral nor automated text-reuse matches on DharmaNexus identify any Pali-internal passages or cross-language parallels for this text [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
